errors: pipe.mjs size table first used an object keyed by nominal size; JS orders integer-like keys ('1','2') first, so sizes came out of order. Caught in the first run of the example, switched to an array.
First upsizing loop could never fire under a uniform friction rate (the tightest path sets the rate, so every end already passes); replaced with an optional trim pass that is reachable and tested.

doc_friction.issue: Post front-matter limits (description <= 160, seo_title <= 70) surfaced one at a time: the first failed in the 5-minute build stage, and the second only on rerun. Checking every front-matter field in stage 1b would save a build cycle.

'Calculators are a poor use of a run' sits uneasily with the construction direction's engineering tools (hvac-load-calc, continuous-beam-calculator). It is unclear where an algorithmic sizing tool falls; I judged it depth, not a calculator.

notes: Idea: water supply pipe sizing from first principles, built on Hunter's 1940 binomial demand worked exactly for mixed fixtures by convolution, plus a pipe tree with a pressure walk and trim. Verified against BMS65 Table 2 from the NIST scan (13/14 rows to 4 dp). Finding: the exact 1% tail rule steps up before Hunter's table (99 vs 107 flush valves for m=8). Checks: run_venture_tests (2 suites ok), venture-preflight full build clean, optout-persistence 20/20, router validate and sync_tree_counts --check clean, Chromium at 1280/390 px with no console errors.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an engineer re-deriving Hunter from BMS65, writing and testing the convolution and pipe-tree sizer, a page, explainer and post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
